script.base: The book has Indianapolis laying 6.5 with a 25.0-18.5 implied score and a moderate 43.5 total, so the base flow is a one-score Colts lead rather than a shootout or a 13-10 slog. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor (58 carries and 208 rush yards over weeks 3-5, about 19.3 carries and 3.59 YPC) get the ball late to protect a lead, but they are running into a Titans defense that allows only 3.78 YPC, so Taylor's extra carries do not automatically become a 90-yard rushing day. Cam Ward, already a low-volume rusher (6 carries, 31 yards L3), trails and throws: Carnell Tate is the air-yards engine (26 targets, 209 yards, 375 air yards in weeks 3-5) and Wan'Dale Robinson is the underneath complement (23 targets, 129 yards, 151 air yards). Tony Pollard's 47 carries and 174 rush yards over those three weeks get trimmed in the fourth quarter if the Titans are behind. Both defenses blitz only about 20-22 percent, so the game is base coverage, not a blitz fest.
script.flip1: Tennessee stays within a score or leads. Pollard keeps a full carry load against an Indianapolis run defense allowing 5.21 YPC with LB Jaylon Carlies out, Taylor never gets the clock-killing fourth quarter, and both passing games stay live so Tate, Robinson, Josh Downs (267 air yards L3) and Tyler Warren (if his groin allows) all stay in the script. This flip helps a Pollard rush over and hurts any assumption that Indianapolis only runs.
script.flip2: Indianapolis is up two scores by halftime. Taylor's late snaps leak to Seth McGowan (15 carries, 61 yards L3; last four rush games 0, 14, 31, 16), Tennessee abandons the run so Pollard's rushing line dies the way a trailing back's line dies, and garbage throws inflate Tate or Colts depth such as Laquon Treadwell. That is the only flip that can push Taylor's carry count through a 3.78 YPC cap, and it puts starter receiving for Indianapolis at risk late.

matchup.shell: No middle-of-field open/closed chart and no man/zone rate are in the pack, so shell is inferred only from blitz splits. Indianapolis blitzes 20 percent and Tennessee 22 percent, so roughly four of five snaps should be base coverage. Tennessee's offense has posted -0.24 EPA per dropback with no blitz versus +0.03 when blitzed, which means the shell Indianapolis will mostly play has been the problem for the Titans' passing game as a team. That does not prove they can erase Tate, but it blocks a strong scheme-fit tag on a Titans receiver over.

Tennessee blitz rate 22 percent: Daniel Jones is -0.11 EPA/db vs blitz and -0.18 vs no blitz, so Indianapolis is slightly less bad when blitzed and negative either way. No sack rate, hurry rate, or time-to-throw is saved. Missing TEN DT Elliott is the only named pass-rush or front absence, and it is a personal scratch, not a confirmed pass-rush collapse.

matchup.overlap: The core overlap is negative for the favorite's run game and positive for the dog's WR1 air yards, with a caveat. Tate is Tennessee's primary target (26 of the listed targets, 375 air yards) and Indianapolis has given up 7.6 to 8.72 YPA plus explosives, but team EPA of -0.24 versus the non-blitz shell cuts against calling that a clean win. Carlies being out overlaps Pollard, Spears and Helm in the short area, which is a receptions/YAC spot this prop menu cannot bet as receptions.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and the Taylor under lost because Elliott's absence and a stacked box that never formed let him rip 24 carries at 4.6 plus a 20-yard screen, matching the week-2 combined 132, while Indianapolis led by 10 and never sat him. That needs a YPC jump above both his own 3.59 and Tennessee's 3.78 plus a receiving spike at the same time. Weeks 3, 4 and 5 landed 72, 97 and 82. The counter is why this is a lean, not a strong, but it is not stronger than the cushion, so the leg stays and is flagged for a human. Tate's counter is harsher: week 5 was 6 yards, Indianapolis can play the non-blitz shell that has produced -0.24 EPA per Titans dropback, and there is no price, so a blank or a -140 tag both lose. That counter is strong enough that Tate is a lean flag, not a bet to size.
slip_story: One base-script stack only: Indianapolis leads a moderate 43.5 game by about a score, Tennessee's run defense caps Taylor under 112.5 rush-plus-receiving, and Tennessee throws to stay in it so Tate's air-yard role is the correlate if a price appears. Do not add Pollard rush over, which needs Tennessee to keep handing him the ball against the 5.21 YPC defense, and do not add Indianapolis receiver overs that need the Colts to keep throwing after they lead. No touchdown legs, one market per player, and no same-game total under mixed with these. Weather cannot be used as a third leg because it was not saved.
